story: I paid Rs 50,50,000 to a car dealer in Mohali, Punjab on 10 January 2026 for a luxury car. The booking was cancelled by the dealer and they have not refunded me.

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 10 Jan 2028 (428 days left). This counts 2 years from 10 Jan 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 5,050,000, so the complaint goes to the State Consumer Commission, with a fee from the official table. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You paid Rs 50,50,000 to a car dealer in Mohali, Punjab on 10 January 2026 for a luxury car. The dealer cancelled the booking and has not refunded the money. You can file a consumer complaint to get your money back.

claims.text: You are a 'consumer' under the Consumer Protection Act because you bought the car for personal use, not for resale or commercial purpose.
The dealer refusing to take back the cancelled booking and refund your Rs 50,50,000 is an unfair trade practice.
The dealer's refusal to refund your money within 30 days of the cancellation is a service deficiency.
Because you paid Rs 50,50,000, your case belongs in the State Consumer Commission, not the District Commission.
You must file your complaint within 2 years from 10 January 2026. Do not wait until the last day.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the car dealer's grievance officer asking for your refund.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step that often resolves the issue before going to a commission.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
next_steps.why: They can help mediate the dispute and guide you on the next steps.

next_steps.action: File a consumer complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in or at the State Consumer Commission.
next_steps.why: This is the official way to legally demand your Rs 50,50,000 refund.

support.text: You are a 'consumer' under the Consumer Protection Act because you bought the car for personal use, not for resale or commercial purpose.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as any person who buys goods for consideration, including a user with approval, but explicitly excludes a person who obtains goods for resale or for any commercial purpose. The sentence states the person bought the car for personal use, not for resale or commercial purpose, which directly aligns with the definition and exclusion in the law text.

support.text: The dealer refusing to take back the cancelled booking and refund your Rs 50,50,000 is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days' is an unfair trade practice. The sentence describes the exact scenario of refusing to take back and refund, which matches the quoted law text.

support.text: The dealer's refusal to refund your money within 30 days of the cancellation is a service deficiency.
support.reason: The law text defines 'deficiency' as any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance required to be maintained by or under any law or undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service, including deliberate withholding of relevant information. The dealer's refusal to refund within 30 days of cancellation can be characterized as a deficiency in service performance, as the law text's definition covers inadequacy in the manner of performance of services.

support.text: Because you paid Rs 50,50,000, your case belongs in the State Consumer Commission, not the District Commission.
support.reason: The law text states 'District Commission: consideration paid up to Rs 50 lakh. State Commission: above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore.' The sentence states the amount is Rs 50,50,000 (which is Rs 50.5 lakh, i.e., above Rs 50 lakh), so the case belongs in the State Consumer Commission, not the District Commission. The amount computation is applied from the rule, which is permitted.

support.text: You must file your complaint within 2 years from 10 January 2026. Do not wait until the last day.
support.reason: The law text states the complaint must be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen. The sentence states 'within 2 years from 10 January 2026' - assuming the cause of action arose on 10 January 2024, this aligns with the two-year limit. The instruction to not wait until the last day is practical advice and does not add a legal time limit, amount cap, right, penalty or condition beyond what the law text contains.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 10 January 2026 I paid Rs 5,050,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 5,050,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the State Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
